data.one_liner: Responsive layout, themed controls, and motion based on parent width.
data.what_it_does: Provides parent-width responsive scoping, bootstrap-like grid columns, themed UI controls, smooth pointer-wheel scrolling, and motion utilities. It measures the parent container rather than the entire screen.
use_when: You need responsive columns and visibility that adapt to parent container widths rather than screen size
You want themed UI controls like buttons, alerts, and accordions built around Material 3
You want smooth scrolling for pointer wheels and re-exported motion components
avoid_when: You prefer standard screen-width responsive frameworks
You only need state management or networking without UI components
strengths: Layout follows parent width instead of screen width
Includes a comprehensive set of themed UI components and smooth scrolling utilities
Mobile-first responsive span and value management
weaknesses: Ties you into its own specific component and layout ecosystem
Requires learning proprietary widget wrappers like NextScope and NextSpan

alternatives.name: responsive_framework
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need traditional screen-scale responsiveness and automatic UI scaling across different screen sizes.

alternatives.name: responsive_builder
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer screen-based breakpoint builders instead of parent-scoped sizing.
